as_of_note: US closes for Tue 27 Oct 2026, day 1 of the FOMC meeting: second straight gain on a chip rally. S&P 500 +0.60% to 7,722.60, Nasdaq +1.18%, Dow +0.03%, Russell 2000 +1.16%. Broadcom +4% on a $63B bank/Blackstone financing for Broadcom tech leased to Anthropic; AMD +5.5%, MU +2.8%; Boeing ~-10.7% on a wider loss and delivery-goal cut. 10Y 4.992% (+0.4bp), 2Y 4.735% (+2.6bp); DXY 102.38 (+0.36%); WTI $99.90 (-1.83%), Brent $113.88 (-1.67%) on Iran peace-condition headlines; Comex gold $4,058.80 (+0.91%). Conference Board confidence 91.7 vs ~81 expected; durable goods +1.8%; new home sales 676k. Hold odds ~92%, Dec hike ~83%. After hours: NXPI -9%, STX -6%, HOOD -5%, ENPH -14%, PPG +7%. Evening futures flat.

mood.reason: Second straight gain led by chips (SOX +3.6%) after Broadcom's $63B Anthropic-linked financing; NYSE advancers led ~1.8 to 1, VIX -4.7% to 17.52, oil below $100, and confidence/durables beat. Tempered by a flat Dow, Boeing's slide, energy and defensives lower, a firmer dollar and hawkish-hold risk ahead of the Fed and Big Tech earnings.

risks: Hawkish hold: Warsh signalling further hikes (Dec hike ~83% priced) with the 10Y pinned just under 5%
Big Tech capex and financing: MSFT and GOOGL Wed, AMZN Thu; BofA says options underprice megacap earnings blowups (via @zerohedge)
Chip bounce fragility: BTIG's Krinsky says fade it, citing SOX patterns seen in 1995 and March 2000
Middle East: Iran insists on its conditions (blockade, sanctions, Hormuz control); a tanker hit mines near Hormuz; US forces reportedly ready to act within 96 hours of an order
Sell-the-news on beats: STX -6%, NXPI -9% after hours despite in-line or better numbers
Midterms next week and Israel's election outcome adding headline risk
